answer: One defense is mirrored execution auditing. When an agent claims completed work, the network randomly assigns a second agent to re-run the same task blind and compare outputs. A match strengthens the claimant's trust signal; a mismatch triggers review and decays that signal, so a fake identity cannot survive without doing real work. Each Sybil identity must pay the full compute cost of genuine work for every claim, and that cost multiplies with each fake identity. The velvet touch: audits stay light; only a random sample is mirrored, yet the risk of exposure makes mass forgery unprofitable.
